models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light and benign overnight at Santa Marina; leave Salina by 06:00-08:00 tomorrow, thunderstorms flagged from midday.
briefing.synopsis: No organised gradient over the Aeolians - winds across all islands are running 3-7 kt and rotating through most of the compass between model hours, which is a slack, thermally driven pattern rather than a synoptic flow. ECMWF IFS and AIFS (both 08 Oct 06Z) and ICON-2i (08 Oct 12Z) agree on the light picture through tomorrow morning, with Salina turning W around 5.7 kt at 06:00 then N/NNE and falling under 3 kt by midday. Through tomorrow afternoon and into Saturday the sea state builds slowly - Salina total wave 0.6 ft now, 1.5 ft by 12:00, 2.0 ft by 18:00 Friday and 2.4 ft Saturday midday - with convective showers signalled in the Friday afternoon windows.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Porto Santa Marina Salina is the recommendation and is scored sheltered (0.909); Rinella is effectively the same at 0.894, so the choice does not matter tonight. Expect SSW 3.6 kt with 0.5 ft SSW swell at the berth (ECMWF IFS/AIFS, 08 Oct 06Z consensus) - Santa Marina is open to the SSW sector but there is nothing in that swell to work on. One oddity: the 18:00 Salina figure carries a 45.5 kt interval-maximum gust against a 4.8 kt mean, which is a light-air model artefact rather than a forecast squall, but if you see a genuine convective cell build, Rinella gives you ESE-facing shelter instead.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Friday morning is the window. Salina 06:00 shows W 5.7 kt, gusting 13.8, wave 0.8 ft; by 12:00 the breeze drops to 3.0 kt from the NNW and the sea begins building. The leg verdict is go for departures at 06:00, 08:00 and 10:00 and it deteriorates after 11:00, so the recommended start is 06:00 - motoring or a very soft broad reach for most of it.

passage_notes.note: 24 nm, 156°T. 06:00 departure: W 5.7 kt, gust 13.8, 0.8 ft, broad reach at 106° TWA, arrive 10:00 - rated go. 08:00 and 10:00 starts also rate go (6.0 kt WNW / 5.0 kt N, 0.8-1.1 ft), though the 08:00 window carries a 25.3 kt interval-max gust against a 6 kt mean. The 12:00 and 14:00 departures are rated no-go, on thunderstorms in the window rather than on wind or sea - waves 1.7-1.9 ft. Portorosa Marina is enclosed, all-round shelter, scored 1.0, with 3.5 kt SE on arrival.

cautions: Thunderstorms are forecast in the Friday midday and afternoon passage windows - both the 12:00 and 14:00 departures are rated no-go on that basis alone. Treat 11:00 as the hard back-stop for leaving Salina.

Large gust-to-mean ratios throughout (45.5 kt at Salina 18:00 today, 37.3 kt at Panarea, 25.3 kt in the 08:00 passage window). These are interval-maximum gusts from IFS/ICON-2i in very light air and are reported, not treated as cautions - but they do indicate an unstable airmass that can produce real convective downdraughts.
Sea state builds behind us: Salina swell 0.5 ft tonight to 1.8 ft by Friday evening, 2.4 ft total wave Saturday midday. Anyone considering a later or alternative leg should factor that in.
Models disagree by more than 6 kt at several points - Filicudi Friday midday spans 1.2-12.2 kt and Portorosa Saturday evening spans 3.2-18.4 kt. Those are genuine spreads, not a mean to plan on.
briefing.confidence_note: Models agree closely on magnitude for the next 24 h (mean wind shift 1.2 kt run-to-run at 0-24 h lead), but mean direction shift of 20-29° in such light air and the convective signal from midday Friday keep this short of high.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
